concerns.text: FR-007 requires an 'input permutation framework' (shuffling effect_size/sample_size) to generate a null distribution. The plan's 'Technical Context' and 'Project Structure' mention 'robustness.py' for permutations, but the 'Tasks' section (implied by the kickback concerns) and 'Complexity Tracking' only explicitly detail the 'year' permutation (FR-004). There is no explicit plan element (phase, task, or data-model entity) dedicated to the distinct 'input permutation' logic required by FR-007 and US-3. The plan risks conflating the two or omitting the input permutation entirely.

FR-006 requires 'inverse-variance weighting with heterogeneity adjustment (DerSimonian-Laird) to combine residual power drift estimates across fields'. The plan's 'Complexity Tracking' mentions DerSimonian-Laird, but the 'Project Structure' and 'Data Flow' do not define an artifact or task to produce the necessary 'field-specific slopes' (stratified estimates) required as input for this aggregation. The global LMM (T012) produces a single slope, not the per-field slopes needed for FR-006. A plan element to extract/fit field-specific models is missing.

FR-009 requires visualization of 'residual power vs. year'. The plan's 'Project Structure' lists 'visualize.py' and 'data/derived/residuals.csv' in the data flow, but the 'Tasks' section (referenced in kickback) indicates T013 depends on an artifact (`residuals.csv`) that is not explicitly produced by a preceding task in the plan's sequence. The plan lacks a clear task definition for generating the `residuals.csv` file from the LMM output before visualization.

SC-005 requires measuring the observed drift slope against a null distribution generated by permuting input variables. This is the success criterion for FR-007. Since FR-007 lacks a corresponding plan element (task/phase) to execute this specific permutation, SC-005 has no corresponding plan element to measure success against. The implementer will have no task to satisfy this success criterion.

SC-004 requires measuring aggregated evidence against the primary mixed-model slope. This depends on FR-006 (aggregation). As FR-006 lacks a plan element to generate the required field-specific inputs for aggregation, SC-004 is unbacked. The plan does not define how the 'aggregated evidence' will be computed or measured.
